sections.label: COVID-19 election contingency plans
sections.summary: The Parliamentary Elections (COVID-19 Special Arrangements) Bill is part of contingency plans letting the Elections Department make temporary arrangements for safe elections during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Parliamentary Elections (COVID-19 Special Arrangements) Bill forms part of the contingency plans to allow the Elections Department (ELD) to implement temporary arrangements for safe elections amid the COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: Excusing voters from voting
sections.summary: Clause 3 excuses voters issued with a Quarantine Order, Stay-Home Notice at home or medical certificate for acute respiratory infection from not voting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Clause 3 excuses voters issued with QO, SHN at home or MC for ARI for not voting.

sections.label: Polling for SHN facilities
sections.summary: Clauses 4 and 5 authorise temporary polling arrangements for persons on Stay-Home Notice at designated facilities to vote outside their electoral divisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Clauses 4 and 5 cater to persons on SHN at designated facilities by authorising temporary polling arrangements for them to vote outside their electoral divisions, either at special polling stations in the SHN designated facilities or some other suitable premises.

sections.label: Representative filing nomination papers
sections.summary: Clause 9 lets an aspiring candidate authorise a representative to file nomination papers if unable or unfit due to quarantine, Stay-Home Notice, hospitalisation or ill-health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Clause 9 allows an aspiring candidate to authorise a representative to file his or her nomination paper on his or her behalf, if the aspiring candidate is unable or unfit to do so because of QO, SHN, hospitalisation or ill-health.

sections.label: Powers for safe General Election
sections.summary: The Bill gives the Elections Department and Returning Officer additional powers for special arrangements at the next General Election under COVID-19, and is unrelated to its timing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Bill aims to protect voters, candidates and election officials at the next General Election by providing the Elections Department and the Returning Officer with additional powers to make special arrangements to deal with running a general election under the COVID-19 situation, on top of the powers in sections 56A to 56F of the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: While this Bill enables the Elections Department and the Returning Officer to make contingency plans for the next General Election, which must be held within a year from now, the Bill is unrelated to the timing of the General Election.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister will decide when to call the election, considering the challenges confronting our country and the evolving COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: Safe voting, core principles
sections.summary: The Bill allows special provisions during the General Election to ensure safe voting while abiding by core principles such as secret voting and one-man-one-vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given the current COVID-19 crisis and without the certainly how long it would last, this Bill will allow special provisions to be made during the General Elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It will ensure that voting to be done safely while abiding with the core principles of the Parliamentary Elections Act such as voting in secret and allowing a Singaporean voter to exercise his rights to a one-man-one-vote principle.

sections.label: Special polling stations in boarding premises
sections.summary: Clause 5 lets Returning Officers set up special polling stations in boarding or other suitable premises for electors under COVID-19 stay orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, clause 5 allows Returning Officers to set up special polling stations in boarding premises or in some other suitable premises in Singapore where the electors are not allowed to leave due to COVID-19 stay orders.

sections.label: Exception to dissuading voters
sections.summary: Clause 8 makes an exception for the Returning Officer and Director of Medical Services to authorise persuading symptomatic or possibly infected voters not to vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, under section 81(1) of the Parliamentary Elections Act, no one can dissuade a voter from voting, from Nomination Day to Polling Day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, under clause 8 of this new Bill, it makes an exception for the Returning Officer and the Director of Medical Services to authorise actions persuading voters not to vote, if they happen to be displaying acute respiratory symptoms, are feverish, or may have been infected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Workers' Party support and queries
sections.summary: The Workers' Party asks what virus progress is needed before a General Election and supports the Bill while raising queries and concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government clarify what progress needs to be made on the virus front before a General Election will be held?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party will support the Bill but I have some queries and concerns about how the provisions will be operationalised.

sections.label: Absent voters and election outcome
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify the Elections Department's commitment to voters under Quarantine or Stay-Home Orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A significant percentage of absent voters may affect the outcome of the poll, especially in a close contest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would like the Minister to clarify what commitment the Elections Department (ELD) is making to voters under Quarantine or Stay-Home Orders.

sections.label: Safeguards for ballot papers and buses
sections.summary: The speaker asks what safeguards protect marked ballot papers and notes the Returning Officer may arrange dedicated buses for electors under Stay-Home Orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What safeguards will there be to ensure that the marked ballot paper is not tampered with or lost and has been duly included for counting?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Explanatory Statement to the Bill, it may become necessary for the Returning Officer (RO) to arrange for dedicated buses to convey electors subject to COVID-19 Stay-Home Orders to the special polling stations that are not their places of accommodation, in order for them to cast their votes.

sections.label: Safeguards on buses and polling booths
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Elections Department will implement safeguards on buses and issue masks, hand sanitisers and gloves, and disinfect polling booths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, will the ELD implement any safeguards to prevent any attempt to influence voters on these buses from any person or even amongst the voters themselves, for example, by recording the journeys on CCTV or by imposing strict no-communications rules on board?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will they be issued with masks, hand sanitisers and gloves and would polling booths be disinfected regularly, as was done in the South Korean election?

sections.label: Campaign rule changes publicity
sections.summary: Changes to campaign rules, such as online video streaming or television time, should be made known publicly and to political parties early so candidates can prepare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, there may possibly be live streaming of videos on the Internet or more television time for candidates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is important for these changes to campaign rules to be made known publicly and to political parties as soon as possible, so that candidates and parties have sufficient time to make necessary preparations and to source for service suppliers.

sections.label: Remote electronic voting alternatives
sections.summary: The speaker seeks the Minister's clarifications on election timing, modified procedures and campaigning, and asks whether the Bill sufficiently explores alternatives like remote electronic voting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I look forward to the Minister's clarifications on the matters I have raised regarding the timing of the General Elections, the modified procedures and campaigning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned whether the Bill goes sufficiently far in exploring alternatives, such as remote electronic voting, that might allow all electors, including those under Quarantine Orders, as well as those falling ill on Polling Day, to vote.

sections.label: Special polling stations for electors
sections.summary: The speaker says clause 5 does not appear to require the Returning Officer to set up special polling stations for all electors on Stay-Home Orders, and the Bill is silent on Quarantine Orders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And it will also mean voters who are acutely sick or under Quarantine Orders, could also exercise their right to vote.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will stand corrected, but the present Bill's clause 5 does not appear to require the Returning Officer (RO) to ensure special polling stations are set up to accommodate all electors subject to Stay-Home Orders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will be helpful if the Government could clarify whether the Bill does impose a requirement that all electors on Stay-Home Orders must be given arrangements to allow them to vote.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The present Bill is also silent on electors under Quarantine Orders, while clause 8 also expressly allows the Returning Officer (RO) or Director of Medical Services to advise electors against voting if they are acutely sick or otherwise exposed to COVID-19.

sections.label: Campaign services and expenditure rules
sections.summary: The speaker proposes regulating essential campaign support services and changing allowed campaign expenditure levels, noting Google stopped accepting political advertising in Singapore from December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, to regulate the extent to which supporting services to a campaign, such as vehicle rental, poster printing, Internet advertising, and so forth, will be made essential, at least to candidates, even if not to other parties.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And fourth, to provide for changes in the allowed campaign expenditure level to account for the fact that much of the work normally done by volunteers on the ground may have to be conducted online through costly advertising, and to account for other increases in cost, as may happen if essential services have to open solely to service candidates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Google, as we know, has ceased to accept political advertising in Singapore, as of December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And with restrictions on physical campaigning, Internet advertising becomes quite essential.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I believe more work can still be done to improve access to voting for all electors and to define rules for campaigning in advance that are fair to all candidates and protect the public health.

sections.label: Three COVID-19 Budgets
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Singapore could be imagined without the three Budgets, which totalled $63.7 billion to fight the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can you imagine a Singapore without the three Budgets, which have kept the economy afloat and supported the livelihood of the people with a total amount of $63.7 billion to fight the COVID-19 crisis?

sections.label: Preparing for safe election
sections.summary: The speaker says 14 April 2021 is still far away and the Bill ensures the Government will take precautions for a fair, safe election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Fourteenth April 2021 is still a long way away, there is no excuse for the Government not to prepare properly for the election in advance and hold one at an appropriate time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This Bill ensures that the Government will put in all the necessary precautions to ensure a fair election and to ensure the safety and health of voters if the outbreak is not over yet.

sections.label: Virtual campaigning and election legitimacy
sections.summary: The passage argues the Bill should allow virtual hustings and rallies and set clear rules against rumours or fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If the electorate feels that some parties were constrained unfairly, then the election will no longer be legitimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Hence, this Bill should make provisions for political parties to conduct virtual hustings and virtual rallies, and to make sure that the boundaries are clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If internet campaigning or social media are used, rules and regulations should be established, especially to guard against any rumours or fake news.

sections.label: Quarantine order voting exemption
sections.summary: Section 3(2) exempts individuals under quarantine orders from voting, and subsection (3) bars quarantined electors from using voting as a defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Materially, section 3(2) of the Bill exempts individuals serving quarantine orders (QOs) from having to vote and subsection (3) makes it clear that quarantined electors cannot claim their right to vote as a valid defence for violating their quarantine order.

sections.label: Numbers under SHNs and QOs
sections.summary: As at 2 May, 2,020 persons were under SHNs and approximately 28,000 under some form of QOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As at 2 May, 2,020 persons were under SHNs and approximately 28,000 under some form of QOs.

sections.label: Zaobao poll and fair campaigning
sections.summary: A late March Lianhe Zaobao poll found 67.5% disagreed with holding an election during the pandemic, and the Minister is asked how fair campaigning will be ensured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I think there was an online dip poll held by Lianhe Zaobao in late March about the desirability of an election found that 67.5% of those polled disagreed on holding an election during the ongoing pandemic as it would be difficult to hold rallies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the Elections Department will ensure commensurate and fair campaigning across all political parties, given the extenuating circumstances?

sections.label: Registered voters and expected turnout
sections.summary: As of 15 April, over 2.6 million voters were registered, and over 1.8 million Singaporeans are expected to head to the polls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of 15 April, there were over 2.6 million voters registered in the voter roll.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The likelihood of such lapses on a day where we expect over 1.8 million Singaporeans to head to the polls is more than high.

sections.label: South Korea reinfection cases
sections.summary: South Korea has seen more than 180 cases where recovered patients became reinfected by the virus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: South Korea, in fact, has seen more than 180 cases where recovered patients have become reinfected by the virus.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment on elections assurance
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to assure that the Bill is a last resort and not a go-ahead to hold elections immediately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some may contend that passing a constitutional amendment with regard to elections would be unprecedented, but Mr Speaker, I think we will all agree that many of us what we have witnessed in this Chamber in the last months have been anything but “business as usual”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to seek the Minister’s assurance that this Bill is viewed as a last resort; that it should only serve as a guarantee, and not be interpreted as a go-ahead to hold elections immediately in this current climate.

sections.label: Bill effect until April 2021
sections.summary: The Bill is intended to have effect until April 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, this Bill is intended to have effect until April 2021.

sections.label: Voting under COVID-19 stay orders
sections.summary: Clause 6(3) lets the Minister make regulations for electors under COVID-19 stay orders to vote without leaving their boarding premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, clause 6(3) provides the Minister with the power to make regulations allowing electors subject to COVID-19 stay orders to vote without leaving their boarding premises.

sections.label: Special polling station hours
sections.summary: Clause 6(2)(b) requires special polling station hours to be at least four hours and close no later than the close of poll in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, clause 6(2)(b) provides that the hours of any poll at a special polling station must not be less than four hours as set by the Returning Officer, and must close no later than the close of poll on polling day in Singapore.

sections.label: Overseas registration centres in 2015
sections.summary: As of 2015, there were 10 overseas registration centres in Canberra, London, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, Dubai, New York, San Francisco and Washington DC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, as of 2015, there were 10 overseas registration centres in Canberra, London, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, Dubai, New York, San Francisco and Washington DC.

sections.label: Right to vote preserved
sections.summary: The Bill does not take away anyone's right to vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Bill does not take away any one’s right to vote.

sections.label: Quarantine order voters penalty waiver
sections.summary: Voters on quarantine order or stay-home notice get an adequate reason for not voting and can restore their names without paying the $50 penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As for those on QO, fewer than 1,000 Singaporeans of voting age are on QO as of yesterday, and certainly not as many as Ms Ong asserts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Because voting is compulsory, the Bill makes clear that being on QO or SHN at home provides an adequate reason to them for not voting and these voters will thus be entitled to have their names restored to the relevant register of electors, without paying the $50 penalty.

sections.label: Polling stations in designated facilities
sections.summary: Based on current numbers, no more than a few polling stations are expected to be set up in the designated facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Based on the current numbers, we do not expect more than a few polling stations to be set up in the designated facilities.

sections.label: Safe elections under COVID-19
sections.summary: Experience shows a safe and smooth election under COVID-19 is possible with necessary safety precautions and assured voter safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Their experience shows that it is possible to run a safe and smooth election under COVID-19, provided we have in place the necessary safety precautions and voters are assured of the safety of the election.

sections.label: Elections Department COVID-19 recommendations
sections.summary: The Elections Department will share details nearer the General Elections, including staggered hours, temperature taking, disinfecting booths and gloves, before the elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As the COVID-19 situation is evolving, the Elections Department will share the details nearer the General Elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, the ideas of staggered hours, temperature taking, disinfecting the polling booths more frequently, gloves – all those are part of the study and ELD will make public its recommendations and advice soon, before the elections, to give everybody and every party the necessary time for their preparations.

sections.label: Voter verification and vote secrecy
sections.summary: Verification, voter secrecy and security concerns are why online voting was not chosen at this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to verify the identity of the voter and, yet, at the same time, we have to assure the voter of the secrecy of his vote, which means that he must be assured that it cannot be traced back absolutely to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, this is the fundamental issue which many countries have grappled with and this is also the reason why we have not chosen to go onto an online mode at this point in time, given the concerns of verification, voter secrecy and also the security concerns.

sections.label: Abandoning overseas voting locations
sections.summary: Overseas voting may be abandoned in locations where risks to safety and health make physical polling impossible, as allowed under the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, if there are unacceptable risks to the safety and health of overseas Singaporean voters and election officials, and if the physical conduct of polling in certain overseas locations is not possible, then we may have to abandon overseas voting in those locations as allowed under the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sections.label: Temporary COVID-19 election arrangements
sections.summary: Mr Zainal asked why the Bill's special arrangements are temporary; they address holding an election under the COVID-19 situation, hoped to be temporary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Zainal asked why are the special arrangements provided in the Bill temporary and not permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These arrangements are specifically to deal with the conduct of an election under the COVID-19 situation, which we all hope is temporary.

sections.label: Delaying election unconstitutional, timing decision
sections.summary: Teo Chee Hean said delaying an election beyond April 2021 and appointing a caretaker government is unconstitutional; the Prime Minister decides when to call the General Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon has articulated, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean has explained in his reply to this House on 25 March 2020 that it is unconstitutional to delay an election beyond the required timeframe of April 2021 and for the President to appoint a caretaker government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is not related to the timing of the General Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It will be for the Prime Minister to consider what is in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans and make the decision on when to call the next General Election.
